prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Emoji · 服务状态 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "服务" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 96px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 61px
  col 3: header "可用率" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 61px
  col 4: header "最近事件" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 437px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"An at-a-glance operations dashboard for comparing service health, availability, and recent incidents across five services.","reading":"Readers anchor on the service name in column 1, quickly scan the status icon/word in column 2 and the uptime percentage in column 3, then read column 4 only when they need incident context. Rows should read as service units, while columns 2 and 3 form the fast comparison pair.","groups":["Columns 2 状态 and 3 可用率 belong together as the health metrics: categorical status plus quantitative uptime.","Column 1 服务 is the row identity and anchor for every comparison.","Column 4 最近事件 is supporting narrative, read after status and uptime."],"keep_intact":["Service names: API Gateway, 支付服务, 消息推送, 对象存储, CDN","Status labels and icons: 正常, 降级, 故障","Availability percentages: 99.99%, 99.12%, 99.97%, 97.40%","Timestamps such as 03:12 and identifiers such as 华东 2"],"may_wrap":["Column 4 event descriptions; they are long narrative text and can wrap naturally.","Headers only if unavoidable; service names, status labels, and percentages should not wrap."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [126, 84, 88, 181] · table 480×395px · row heights [39, 39, 92, 66, 92, 66] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [118, 82, 82, 197] · table 480×395px · row heights [39, 39, 92, 66, 92, 66] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [120, 96, 96, 167] · table 480×422px · row heights [39, 39, 118, 66, 92, 66] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
